<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A short-film-sequence loss neither predicts 100,000-event failure nor becomes a local win from online results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2402.17152-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b88d0c3b149bbc6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hstu" data-paper-title="Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6dfb7484be36691">What does M-FALCON share, and why not cache every ranking score?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahstu">Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Section 3.4/Appendix H isolate candidate microbatches and share per-layer candidate-independent history KV. Each candidate still projects and interacts separately. Versions and history constrain reuse; local HSTU omits this serving optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A thousand items can share history while cameras and shoes retain different scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2402.17152-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6dfb7484be36691">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hstu" data-paper-title="Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e74368e779e676f8">How does all-position HSTU training preserve causality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahstu">Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each valid state reads its prefix and predicts the next item; mask padding and invalid targets. One encoding supplies multiple losses. Candidate action interleaving is a separate contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A predicts B and A/B predicts C without A seeing B or C.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hyformer" data-paper-title="HyFormer: Revisiting the Roles of Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-hyformer-d0fa9291" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-2138dbf99ca17a2d">Why initialize HyFormer&#x27;s Global Queries from non-sequence fields and the sequence mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahyformer">HyFormer: Revisiting the Roles of Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The query needs the current global context and a history overview so it can read the long sequence purposefully instead of starting from an unconditional slot. Each decoding step is followed by boosting to combine fields with history. The initial summary can lose details; later reads can help but cannot guarantee complete recovery.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A travel setting and a photography-heavy history can steer the initial query toward lightweight camera needs. A constant query sees the current setting only in a later layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.12681-hyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2138dbf99ca17a2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hyformer" data-paper-title="HyFormer: Revisiting the Roles of Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-64a45769bae35220">Why does HyFormer apply Query Boosting after every history read and pass the queries back to the next layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahyformer">HyFormer: Revisiting the Roles of Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If history is compressed once before field interactions, those interactions cannot change what evidence is read next. HyFormer alternates sequence reads and non-sequence token mixing, letting new evidence enter field interactions and boosted queries return to history. The compact queries and field representations co-evolve; this does not require rewriting the raw history for every candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The first layer finds an outdoor interest. After mixing in rainy weather and item material, the next query can focus on waterproof gear. A one-shot summary followed by an MLP cannot easily ask that new question of the history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.12681-hyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64a45769bae35220">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hyformer" data-paper-title="HyFormer: Revisiting the Roles of Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3b7a374c10d8c91">When do interactions occur in HyFormer&#x27;s query co-evolution versus LONGER followed by RankMixer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahyformer">HyFormer: Revisiting the Roles of Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The serial path summarizes the sequence before field mixing, so the initial history read cannot react to later field results. HyFormer sends boosted queries back for another read, conditioning it over several layers. Earlier interaction adds expressiveness but may also strengthen popularity bias: the source reports a large local increase in head share, not unequivocally better personalization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: One round finds camping signals, field mixing adds a budget constraint, and the next round seeks lightweight gear. A completed one-shot summary generally cannot reread raw history under the new constraint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.12681-hyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3b7a374c10d8c91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:hyformer" data-paper-title="HyFormer: Revisiting the Roles of Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-26d294f33aa7d17b">Why must HyFormer feed the boosted query back into the next cross-attention layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ahyformer">HyFormer: Revisiting the Roles of Sequence Modeling and Feature Interaction in CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reusing the original Q would make each layer repeat the same question and eliminate co-evolution. Sequence K/V, decoded queries, and non-sequence tokens also need aligned layouts; per-token transforms operate on the mixed layout. The local two-query reduction is a specific implementation, not an exact match for production parameters and cache paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The second query should carry the first layer&#x27;s budget and use-case information. If code accidentally reuses Q0, a deeper model can still reduce loss without implementing the paper&#x27;s iterative information loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.12681-hyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26d294f33aa7d17b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:inthq" data-paper-title="IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-inthq-fbf3d84e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ec8aa37e3eb59e97">Why are when, where, how, and via query roles rather than just labels in IntHQ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ainthq">IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Queries extract different evidence from behavior and context streams, affecting intermediate representations instead of merely producing four final predictions. The two streams preserve distinct sources; multilayer interactions connect time, location, manner, and channel. The names suggest specialization, which still needs to be checked.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: When someone returns depends more on intervals, whereas where they go depends more on location history. Two heads attached to the same fixed vector cannot separately guide the early read.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09634-inthq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ec8aa37e3eb59e97">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:inthq" data-paper-title="IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-787bc07ff99b39ff">What does IntHQ gain by using when, where, how, and via queries within multiple encoder layers rather than only four output heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ainthq">IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>With heads only at the end, the encoder may compress every kind of evidence the same way. Task queries read separate behavior and context streams at multiple layers, so the task can guide evidence selection: time can favor periodicity and channel can favor entry points. Shared lower layers can capture common structure, but task conflict does not disappear automatically; verify that the queries really specialize.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: In the same lunchtime search event, the time query cares about a lunch-break pattern and the channel query about search as the entry point. Letting both ask inside the encoder is more flexible than giving each a head on one summary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09634-inthq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-787bc07ff99b39ff">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:inthq" data-paper-title="IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d208b2271a6edac">What structure does IntHQ&#x27;s two-stream interaction preserve compared with concatenating behavior and context once?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ainthq">IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The streams distinguish events from context before task queries read across layers, avoiding undifferentiated mixing from the outset. One concatenation is simpler, but it is harder to track source and task conditions explicitly. Stronger structure does not guarantee results: the local public proxy regressed, and query names cannot replace evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A weekday lunch hour is context; recent restaurant clicks are behavior. The two streams can encode them separately before answering when and where, without forcing both to affect every target equally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09634-inthq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d208b2271a6edac">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:inthq" data-paper-title="IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4176beff76081d52">Why must IntHQ keep the task axis separate from the history axis in multilayer query aggregation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ainthq">IntHQ: Task-Interactive Hierarchical Query on Dual-Stream Representations for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Amap / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Each task query reads the relevant stream or layer&#x27;s K/V and forms a task state. Softmax belongs on the candidate evidence axis. Normalizing over the four tasks as if they were historical records would make tasks compete. Role alignment matters more than matching final dimensions, and the public proxy does not cover all real spatiotemporal tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The when query should distribute weight over historical times, not share a sum of one with the where query; otherwise adding a location task changes the time task&#x27;s evidence budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09634">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.09634-inthq/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4176beff76081d52">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:journeyformer" data-paper-title="JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-journeyformer-09e3e4a3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbedf876ab0f5949">Why encode a guest journey rather than a set of viewed listings in JourneyFormer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ajourneyformer">JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Searches, views, saves, and bookings mark different stages, and elapsed time affects whether a need still applies. Type and time embeddings let the same property mean different things in different paths and jointly represent long- and short-term behavior. Event labels are not causal explanations, and a completed past trip need not match current demand.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A seaside listing booked three months ago and an urban apartment saved today should not count equally as unmet needs. A set of listing IDs loses that distinction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19108">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.19108-journeyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbedf876ab0f5949">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:journeyformer" data-paper-title="JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d64a894bfbe04f44">Why does JourneyFormer encode event types and time in the guest journey rather than just listing viewed properties?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ajourneyformer">JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The same property means different things during search, viewing, saving, and booking. Time gaps distinguish one trip from older plans. A shared journey sequence learns relations between stages while retaining both long-term preferences and immediate travel needs. Caching and sparsity reduce cost but do not relax which events were visible at request time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A user saved a seaside listing last year but now searches downtown and views business apartments. Listing IDs alone do not distinguish the trips; event type and timing can reveal the current one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19108">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.19108-journeyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d64a894bfbe04f44">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:journeyformer" data-paper-title="JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e9c189d7e07fb75f">What does a unified long and short guest journey retain, and what does it cost compared with a recent window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ajourneyformer">JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Long history preserves stable destinations and accommodation preferences, while the short window shows the current trip stage. Joint encoding can connect them but adds attention and update costs, motivating caches and sparsity. Older trips can be stale, and more history need not be more accurate. The source&#x27;s local negative result applies only to its proxy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A family-room preference may remain relevant during a business trip, but the new context also matters. The newest events alone can forget the stable need, while equal weighting of every old trip can distract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19108">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.19108-journeyformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e9c189d7e07fb75f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:journeyformer" data-paper-title="JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d6bbeba9e6d3e71">Why must listing, event type, and time use one version in JourneyFormer&#x27;s incremental cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Ajourneyformer">JourneyFormer: Encoding Airbnb Guest Journey with Sequence Modeling</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Airbnb</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All three determine state, so changing an event type or time encoding makes the old cache inconsistent with new inputs. A causal sequence can contain only events already observed, not future bookings. The local proxy lacks real lodging inventory and full production refreshes, so its latency does not establish online performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If a view is corrected to a booking, a stale cache will still treat the user as exploring and may keep recommending. Refreshing the listing vector alone will not fix the event state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kunlun" data-paper-title="Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-kunlun-7994f8f7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-062a5b981a1264df">Why does Kunlun put a sequence block and an interaction block in the same layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akunlun">Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The sequence block extracts behavioral dependencies and the interaction block combines heterogeneous fields. Global Interaction passes information between layers to prevent isolated towers from hitting a communication bottleneck. HSP summarizes sequence seeds, while system parallelism and CompSkip address deep scaling. Enlarging one FFN does not reproduce these separate mechanisms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: History reveals camping intent, and a budget field in the interaction block changes its interpretation and later fusion. Towers concatenated only at the end see each other&#x27;s clues much later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10016">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10016-kunlun/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-062a5b981a1264df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kunlun" data-paper-title="Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4031a3745258df11">Why interleave sequence and interaction blocks in Kunlun rather than making only one tower larger?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akunlun">Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The sequence model handles historical dependencies and the heterogeneous interaction model handles field relationships. Scaling one side alone can leave the other as an information bottleneck. Kunlun exchanges sequence seeds and non-sequence information between layers, uses gating and residuals to control deep updates, and relies on parallel engineering to scale. Joint structure does not make every module free to reuse: distinguish candidate dependence from serving cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A long history reveals outdoor interest, but price and context interactions arriving only at the end cannot guide deeper interpretation. Interleaving lets them cooperate across layers instead of concatenating once.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10016">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10016-kunlun/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4031a3745258df11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kunlun" data-paper-title="Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-26d7b73cacf6f46c">Where does Kunlun&#x27;s gated GDPA affect evidence compared with ordinary softmax attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akunlun">Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The gate&#x27;s log-sigmoid is added to attention logits, suppressing relations before normalization rather than scaling the final vector afterward. It can suppress noise or rare important events. CompSkip separately changes residual depth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Downweighting an accidental click before normalization reallocates attention to other events; multiplying the whole user vector afterward cannot reproduce that change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10016">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.10016-kunlun/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26d7b73cacf6f46c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:kunlun" data-paper-title="Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f1652e912362ce49">Why must Kunlun&#x27;s CompSkip align the dimensions of the old state and F output?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Akunlun">Kunlun: Establishing Scaling Laws for Massive-Scale Recommendation Systems through Unified Architecture Design</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>h(l+1)=αhl+(1−α)Fl(hl) combines states in the same representation space. Specify the range and broadcast axis of α rather than gating across candidates or batch examples accidentally. Respect synchronized sequence and interaction updates. The four-layer local compact core&#x27;s quality variation is not production throughput evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A per-layer α must not accidentally become candidate-dependent and contaminate a shared state merely because broadcasting succeeds.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lazformer" data-paper-title="LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<span id="paper-recommendation-lazformer-e00dc3de" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9216d984ce591cdc">Why distinguish transferable generative pretraining from the ranking residual adapter in LazFormer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alazformer">LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pretraining learns general sequence and semantic structure. Ranking needs candidate value and serving objectives; the residual adds a task-specific update without rewriting the base. Dense recent and sparse distant inputs and sparse attention separately control history cost. Verify training and serving mechanisms individually.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Pretraining learns a camera-to-lens progression; adaptation adds the current candidate&#x27;s price, a business trade-off not necessarily learned by transfer alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.14978-lazformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9216d984ce591cdc">Question link</a></p>

</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lazformer" data-paper-title="LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a1ae90a18185961">Why keep a ranking residual adapter alongside LazFormer&#x27;s transferable pretrained backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alazformer">LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generative pretraining learns broad sequence patterns, but industrial ranking needs candidate interaction and frequent updates. A residual adds ranking-specific behavior without wholesale overwrite; dense recent and sparse distant tokens with sparse attention control long-history cost. Local deterministic mapping and adapter composition do not reproduce full generative pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The backbone knows long-term consumption, while a promotion needs extra price interactions. A fixed weighted scorer cannot prove the original training pipeline ran.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.14978-lazformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a1ae90a18185961">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lazformer" data-paper-title="LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a9b8ac400463b5cf">What long-range information do dense recent and sparse distant tokens retain versus fixed recent truncation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alazformer">LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Truncation drops old history entirely. The mixed representation keeps coarse older evidence and detailed recent events, and sparse connections lower pairwise cost. Compression can lose rare events. The deterministic mapping and residual in the local version are interfaces, not original long-sequence pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Keep every click from the last two days but summarize last year&#x27;s history by groups. This remembers more than ten recent clicks, yet an important old exception may be lost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.14978">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.14978-lazformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a9b8ac400463b5cf">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:lazformer" data-paper-title="LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0bb2b4577fe253e9">Why must the LazFormer local implementation not report the paper&#x27;s two-week A/B numbers as its own training results?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alazformer">LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce Group</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local version has deterministic candidate scoring, transferable mapping, and a ranking residual with fusion selected on validation. It lacks full large-model training and online serving. Report the negative public-protocol result and separately cite the paper&#x27;s business gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A residual in local movie scores does not imply generative pretraining; copying the paper&#x27;s GMV percentages into local metrics would mix evidence sources.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:linkedin-feed-sr" data-paper-title="An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<span id="paper-recommendation-linkedin-feed-sr-d07e7f6a" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0c37f2494e9faa">Why does LinkedIn Feed combine candidates, interaction history, and context into a sequence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alinkedin-feed-sr">An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They jointly determine current content value, so a common backbone lets evidence interact before the final stage. Very long history retains career interests but adds compute and candidate dependence, motivating incremental serving. A unified representation does not make all states reusable across candidates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Recent job seeking, a long-running interest in engineering, and a current job-listing candidate together explain value better than a set of liked articles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:linkedin-feed-sr" data-paper-title="An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-35861795e0c6722e">Why does LinkedIn Feed&#x27;s sequential model stress evaluation without random negative sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alinkedin-feed-sr">An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A few easy random negatives simplify ranking and conceal hard distinctions in a large pool. A model that jointly processes candidates, history, and context needs a consistent candidate protocol to test scaling and incremental serving. A local proxy is not LinkedIn&#x27;s production distribution, and gains cannot be compared across different negative counts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Finding one positive among nine obviously irrelevant items differs from finding it among thousands of similar Feed candidates, even with the same model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12354">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12354-linkedin-feed-sr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-35861795e0c6722e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:linkedin-feed-sr" data-paper-title="An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-500035993adfd631">Why is evaluation without random negatives harder than testing one positive and a few random negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alinkedin-feed-sr">An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sampled sets often omit real competitors. Metrics vary with negative count and difficulty, potentially overstating ranking ability. A fuller pool better represents serving competition but costs more. Evaluation without random negatives does not imply no training negatives or justify comparing percentages across protocols.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ranking among 99 irrelevant articles is easier than beating many similar articles in the full professional corpus. The metric can be named NDCG in both without measuring the same task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12354">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12354-linkedin-feed-sr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-500035993adfd631">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:linkedin-feed-sr" data-paper-title="An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b6718059174fd2c3">Why validate candidate-independent history state before incremental serving in LinkedIn Feed?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alinkedin-feed-sr">An Industrial-Scale Sequential Recommender for LinkedIn Feed Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A reusable prefix must not depend on the candidate being swapped. History and model changes also invalidate caches. Candidate attention may read shared state but must not reuse candidate-conditioned history for other candidates. The local core proxy lacks the full LinkedIn system and does not measure true long-sequence throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A new article may read old history K/V through a different query. If the old article was written into that state, sharing it with the new one leaks candidate information despite fast execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12354">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12354-linkedin-feed-sr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b6718059174fd2c3">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llatte" data-paper-title="LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<span id="paper-recommendation-llatte-05036174" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a305aa9a8dee1f67">Why scale LLaTTE&#x27;s async long history separately from the online short sequence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allatte">LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The upstream model processes more history and caches an overview. The downstream model uses fresh events and candidate-aware interactions without rerunning the big model on each request. Each stage has a bottleneck, so measure compression and transfer efficiency rather than assuming all upstream gains reach serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A cached profile retains years of interests, while recent baby-product browsing can change ranking immediately instead of waiting for the next refresh.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llatte" data-paper-title="LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b35ec683629a5330">Why does LLaTTE still read recent history with candidate-aware attention after caching LLM user representations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allatte">LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Async long-history encoding supports more compute but refreshes periodically and compresses details. The online short sequence adds recent behavior, and the candidate query picks relevant evidence. Stable knowledge and real-time relevance are distinct responsibilities. Measure transfer of upstream gains downstream instead of assuming all of them survive.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An overnight cache remembers photography, but a new backpack search signals travel. Online history adds the new intent and lets the current candidate read relevant knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.20083-llatte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b35ec683629a5330">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llatte" data-paper-title="LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a3ca85e63b834cce">Why isn&#x27;t LLaTTE&#x27;s transfer efficiency τ just the upstream NE improvement?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allatte">LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A better upstream model need not yield proportional downstream gains: cache size, fusion capacity, and task objectives can discard information. τ compares the two improvements to help decide where to spend compute. A tiny denominator or mismatched protocols makes the ratio unstable; an empirical trend is not a theorem.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: If upstream NE improves and downstream NE barely changes, candidate-aware fusion may be more useful than adding upstream parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.20083-llatte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a3ca85e63b834cce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:llatte" data-paper-title="LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ceb5ad8c87ef2cd">Why can&#x27;t LLaTTE&#x27;s local four latent queries and recent-12 path establish the value of a 2,000-dimensional production cache?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Allatte">LLaTTE: Scaling Laws for Multi-Stage Sequence Modeling in Large-Scale Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The small setup trains long summaries, short history, and gating but does not fully measure production refreshes, roughly 400 online events, or multisource features. Verify gradient flow and candidate dependence, then report the matched short baseline and head exposure. Size differences cannot become measured QPS or conversion gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Four summary vectors reading 24 movie events test information flow, not the latency of a production cache over tens of thousands of multisource events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20083">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.20083-llatte/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ceb5ad8c87ef2cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:long-history-transformer" data-paper-title="Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-long-history-transformer-f4293ee0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eb7894ea434ef53a">Why pair the offline Long-History Transformer cache with a recent online path?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Along-history-transformer">Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Async long history retains stable interests but lags. A small online model reads recent changes and the cache, combining coverage with responsiveness. Compression can lose details, and auxiliary pretraining and ad fine-tuning are distinct stages. Concatenating a long vector does not reproduce all of this.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Baby-product browsing can change a prediction immediately even while the background cache still emphasizes photography.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14331-long-history-transformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eb7894ea434ef53a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:long-history-transformer" data-paper-title="Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-269d7fd18f895962">Why keep recent events in a lightweight online Transformer when a long-history cache already exists?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Along-history-transformer">Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The cache covers stable patterns but refresh lag excludes recent events. A short online window plus cached state responds without re-encoding all history. Auxiliary objectives support both representations. A small cache can lose information; do not mix fresh offline states with stale online caches in evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Overnight history records photography, but today&#x27;s sudden childcare searches need a recent path without waiting for a refresh or re-encoding all past events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14331-long-history-transformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-269d7fd18f895962">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:long-history-transformer" data-paper-title="Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2629bc85bd284c14">What costs move to the background in a two-stage async model compared with request-time full history encoding?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Along-history-transformer">Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The background encodes long history and caches fixed-width state, avoiding repeated long self-attention at serving time. Refresh, storage, invalidation, and compression costs remain. The source lacks actual Yandex feature-store measurements, so structure alone cannot establish latency gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Requests can share a daily summary, but if updates are frequent and requests rare, background compute may not pay off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14331-long-history-transformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2629bc85bd284c14">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:long-history-transformer" data-paper-title="Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1e6ddaa6ed1b5743">How should the local 24-step offline, four-step online model enforce input cutoffs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Along-history-transformer">Long-History User Transformers for Real-Time Ad Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Yandex</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both branches use only events before the prediction. Define overlap handling and never build a cache from the full sequence including test events. Next-item and feedback auxiliary labels stay on the training side. A 32-dimensional cache is a scale-down, not the original history length or feature scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A cache containing the final film leaks it even if the online branch reads only four earlier events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14331">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.14331-long-history-transformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1e6ddaa6ed1b5743">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-longer-50bd52b2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b0338092be4725e">Why isn&#x27;t a LONGER global token a fixed user summary?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Globals can include CLS, user, and candidate fields. Short queries propagate their first-layer states; candidate globals remain request-specific. Cacheability depends on actual dependency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user ID can be shared but a price-derived global belongs to one item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b0338092be4725e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b94e636f79ea884b">Do later LONGER layers keep updating long history after using it as KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The first layer uses short global/recent Q against merged long KV. Output follows Q length; later self-attention runs only on the short states. This is inter-layer compression, not upfront truncation. The local namesake lacks full fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Short query cards inspect a long reference once, then only the cards are refined.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b94e636f79ea884b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5e49e56233e457f1">Where does LONGER compress compared with candidate top-k history?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Top-k discards events before fine encoding. LONGER lets short queries read merged long KV once, then propagates short output. Merging is still lossy and the local first-layer path is not fully faithful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read a broad compressed source once rather than discard all but ten pages up front.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5e49e56233e457f1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f90aa5aa39428720">Why can larger LONGER merge factor K fail to reduce total FLOPs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Section 3.4 shortens positions while widening merged features, increasing projection cost but reducing attention cost. InnerTrans supplies within-group interaction. This is not fixed-width mean pooling or monotone quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Moving from four to eight events per wider token can make matrix work rebound.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f90aa5aa39428720">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-906a6ef0a4addaf4">How cache user KV if some global tokens contain candidates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sections 3.5.2/3.6.3 mask candidate-specific globals from user sequences. Cache independent user KV and compute candidate query outputs separately. Global means aggregation role, not independence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two products share behavior KV but use distinct globals; do not cache a user state already conditioned on product A for B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-906a6ef0a4addaf4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:longer" data-paper-title="LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1fb09578a44894ee">Why verify first-layer Q length and subsequent state length?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Alonger">LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The defining path is short global/recent Q over long KV, then short-only self-attention. Concatenating every input and self-attending each layer changes information flow. Inspect actual shapes and masks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With KV length 500 and Q length 100, the next layer should receive 100 positions, not over 600.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04421">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2505.04421-longer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1fb09578a44894ee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mdl" data-paper-title="MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mdl-daad794f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
