<h2 id="qa-f6f40c7f4f0b55d9">Why turn scenario and task into tokens in MDL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amdl">MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They determine which field relations matter, not only which head to use. Domain-feature attention lets scenario queries read features deep in the model, and task tokens and aggregation form specific outputs. Token roles permit interaction but do not ensure intended semantics emerge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A user&#x27;s features matter differently for live shopping and short-video viewing. A scenario token can adjust intermediate reads, not just swap the final classifier.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.07520-mdl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6f40c7f4f0b55d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mdl" data-paper-title="MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4f1ac6ba42c0ed1">Why tokenize scenario and task in MDL rather than just choosing output heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amdl">MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late heads cannot continuously steer feature selection. Tokens let domain queries read relevant fields across layers and task information shape shared representations. Deeper sharing may cause interference; check whether low-traffic settings are overridden by larger ones instead of assuming a unified design helps all tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Home-page clicks and search conversion may need different product evidence. Scenario and task tokens can change early reads instead of splitting one summary at the end.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.07520-mdl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4f1ac6ba42c0ed1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mdl" data-paper-title="MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc0887908bac6b4c">How does MDL&#x27;s deep domain-feature interaction condition more than a shallow gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amdl">MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shallow gate adjusts already encoded features. Deep interaction repeatedly conditions representation formation, expanding joint modeling at higher compute and negative-transfer risk. Local accuracy improved with a clear rise in head exposure, not evidence that every group benefited.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: The scenario can emphasize price first and combine it with budget next. A shallow gate can only reweight previously formed interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.07520-mdl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc0887908bac6b4c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mdl" data-paper-title="MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7411c8a5b2cb6b28">Why label feature, scenario, and task token identities in MDL?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amdl">MDL: A Unified Multi-Distribution Learner in Large-scale Industrial Recommendation through Tokenization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal final dimensions do not make evidence, conditions, and predictions interchangeable. Keep attention layout and readout positions aligned. Treating scenario count as batch size or reading the wrong task position silently changes the objective. The local 19 scenarios are proxies, not 19 production businesses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A purchase token cannot supervise viewing just because both are two-dimensional; verify identity mapping as well as shape.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07520">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.07520-mdl/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7411c8a5b2cb6b28">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memento" data-paper-title="Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-memento-1c9d9291" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-91698d7766f5d11a">Why are Representation Memento and Data Memento different memory stores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemento">Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Representation memory retrieves long-term user evidence for a current prediction. Data memory finds forgotten examples related to the current batch and updates parameters again. Storage, updating, and evaluation differ, so implementing either does not complete both loops.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reading old photography history today is representation memory. Replaying training examples to prevent forgetting a user segment is data memory.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24051">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.24051-memento/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91698d7766f5d11a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memento" data-paper-title="Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1cdd545af184e84">What types of forgetting do Memento&#x27;s representation and data-replay paths address?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemento">Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Truncated inference history loses distant interests; the representation path retrieves relevant nonredundant events and conditions predictions. Single-use training samples can be forgotten through parameter updates; the data path replays old samples related to the current batch. Local history retrieval does not validate both paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieve last year&#x27;s photography click as input; replay old training examples to relearn a rare category. Reading an old vector is not training replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24051">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.24051-memento/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1cdd545af184e84">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memento" data-paper-title="Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0af300afefe60c1">How does query-conditioned MMR in Memento trade relevance and redundancy against LastN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemento">Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>LastN uses recency; MMR picks query-relevant events while avoiding duplicates of already selected history. It can recover distant evidence but depends on query quality, with λ balancing relevance and coverage. Local results cover retrieval, not Ember or data replay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Ten recent lens views are redundant; MMR can keep one and retrieve an older camera-use event, or choose poorly if the query is wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24051">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.24051-memento/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0af300afefe60c1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:memento" data-paper-title="Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6291b49903b2a5c">Why can&#x27;t Memento&#x27;s local metrics verify Ember transformations and data replay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amemento">Memento: Personalized RAG-Style Long-Retention Data Scaling for Online Ads Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only Representation Memento&#x27;s MMR ran. Ember affine/quadratic transforms, production retrieval, and historical replay were not reproduced. Broader claims need learned conditional parameters, actual replay updates, and matched controls. Choose λ on validation, not test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Better NDCG after recovering an old photography event supports input evidence, not claims about forgetting after SGD without replay updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24051">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.24051-memento/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6291b49903b2a5c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mixformer" data-paper-title="MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mixformer-c586b532" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3c5d69fa3b41645">Why include both dense fields and behaviors in MixFormer&#x27;s unified token space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amixformer">MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate encoders postpone communication. Joint layers update both representations and scale their capacity together. Heterogeneous fields need proper projection, not treatment as literal words. Serving still separates user and candidate dependencies; not every state can be shared.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A rain field helps interpret outdoor clicks early, and the refined interest feeds back into field interactions before any final concatenation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.14110-mixformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3c5d69fa3b41645">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mixformer" data-paper-title="MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7b0558ebad0e78da">How does MixFormer&#x27;s shared token space change information flow versus concatenating two towers at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amixformer">MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late concatenation finishes field interactions and sequence encoding separately. MixFormer updates both token types together across layers and scales joint modeling. Serving can still decouple reusable user computation from candidate-dependent work rather than rerunning all user history per candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A rainy setting can shape early interpretation of outdoor browsing and reinforce waterproof needs across layers, while late fusion sees two completed summaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.14110-mixformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7b0558ebad0e78da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mixformer" data-paper-title="MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1bc780cf4206ff6c">Why does a parameter-matched stacked baseline isolate MixFormer&#x27;s architecture better than the old fixed semantic gate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amixformer">MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actually train stacked and unified models with similar budgets to compare interaction structure. A fixed score gate only proxies fusion. Matching parameters does not remove optimization, feature, or variance differences. The source retired the old proxy; do not mix its numbers with the new experiment or claim stable industrial gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Comparing two trained architectures is meaningful; adding a semantic constant to existing scores tests a rule, not unified Transformer training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.14110-mixformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1bc780cf4206ff6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mixformer" data-paper-title="MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd3913255c1e2934">Why check whether candidates enter the shared backbone before reusing one MixFormer user encoding for all dot products?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amixformer">MixFormer: Co-Scaling Up Dense and Sequence in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>If a candidate modifies the unified user state, swapping it invalidates reuse. The local model jointly encodes user fields and history first, then scores separate candidate vectors. Verify actual dependencies, not naming. Public genres replacing private fields also limit fidelity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Encode four user fields and 32 events once and dot-product with shoes or a camera. If the camera went into the backbone, reusing that state for shoes would change the path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14110">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.14110-mixformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd3913255c1e2934">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ml-dcn" data-paper-title="ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ml-dcn-5baa5b42" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-780a90dec56504ba">Why mask the cross input rather than the final score in ML-DCN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aml-dcn">ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Selecting channels before multiplication changes which interactions form. Scaling a final score cannot undo bad crosses. Low rank separately controls internal width. Learned mask values are not causal importance and do not prove low-weight features can be removed everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Suppressing noisy price before interaction prevents bad combinations; scaling the final prediction suppresses useful signals too.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09194-ml-dcn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-780a90dec56504ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ml-dcn" data-paper-title="ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8e34d21c8c29d9b">Why apply both low-rank projection and a learned mask before ML-DCN&#x27;s explicit crosses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aml-dcn">ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-width crosses increase compute with capacity. Low rank maps to a configurable small dimension and back; the mask selects participating channels. These control cost and information separately. Residuals preserve the original state, but a low-rank bottleneck can still miss relationships outside its subspace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rather than fully crossing thousands of age, city, and device features, select useful channels and combine them in tens of dimensions, leaving budget for depth.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09194-ml-dcn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8e34d21c8c29d9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ml-dcn" data-paper-title="ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e8d71d1a1a2da70a">How do rank and channel selection trade expressiveness against DCN-V2&#x27;s full cross matrix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aml-dcn">ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A full matrix expresses more general transformations. Low rank constrains the subspace while masks select channels adaptively and save capacity budget. More layers need not restore omitted relations. The shared local scorer proxy is not a full parameter-matched DCN-V2 control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Compressing a thousand dimensions to dozens saves compute but can lose rare geography–category relationships that masks cannot recreate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09194-ml-dcn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e8d71d1a1a2da70a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ml-dcn" data-paper-title="ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7f87b3e0f77bd8f8">What shape relationships should ML-DCN&#x27;s V, U, mask, and x0 satisfy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aml-dcn">ML-DCN: Masked Low-Rank Deep Crossing Network Towards Scalable Ads Click-through Rate Prediction at Pinterest</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mask the current xl channelwise, map with V to the internal rank, use U to map back, multiply by original x0, then add residual and bias. Do not replace x0 with xl each layer or broadcast the mask across the batch axis incorrectly. Verify gradient flow instead of using fixed selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Rank 32 does not make the output 32-dimensional; it must project back before the elementwise x0 product.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09194">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.09194-ml-dcn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7f87b3e0f77bd8f8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mlcc" data-paper-title="Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-mlcc-9b40fb24" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5652f96f3280d4b4">Why project MLCC&#x27;s compact-space crosses back into a high-dimensional backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amlcc">Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compact z saves interaction cost, while the residual backbone retains old information. Projection P injects new combinations rather than trapping all layers in one reduced space. Compression may omit directions, and residuals do not guarantee learning every high-order cross.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Compute budget–category interaction in a small space and add it back, leaving other fields available at the next layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12041-mlcc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5652f96f3280d4b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mlcc" data-paper-title="Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f3168e9435168fe">Why compress before every explicit cross in MLCC instead of compressing only the initial input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amlcc">Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Layer states contain different interaction orders. Recompressing the current state lets the next cross use newly formed information. Dynamic crosses in compact space project back into the backbone to reduce high-dimensional cost. Parallel subspaces can cover different relations but need to retain useful directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: First combine region and category, then compress that combination to cross it with price preference. Reusing only initial fields misses the new relationship.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12041-mlcc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f3168e9435168fe">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mlcc" data-paper-title="Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-acd8a77f6ca3a463">How do MC-MLCC&#x27;s parallel subspaces differ from widening one compression space?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amlcc">Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate subspaces can specialize in distinct crosses and combine outputs; one wider projection concentrates capacity. Parallel channels can specialize or duplicate each other. Match parameters and FLOPs; the mechanism does not establish universal cost and accuracy gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Price–budget and time–context can occupy different channels, but if both learn popularity, capacity is redundant.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12041-mlcc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-acd8a77f6ca3a463">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:mlcc" data-paper-title="Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e302b2505b1994e">Why must MLCC&#x27;s Cl and Pl match the corresponding layer state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amlcc">Compress, Cross and Scale: Multi-Level Compression Cross Networks for Efficient Scaling in Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Bilibili</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compress current xl to z, compute its dynamic gate from z, and project back to xl&#x27;s width. Reusing the initial compression or the wrong layer&#x27;s weights weakens progressive high-order updates. Check that each layer actually receives the updated state, not just valid residual shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Layer two should compress a state that includes layer one&#x27;s crosses; compressing x0 again can just repeat the first cross.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12041">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.12041-mlcc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e302b2505b1994e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msn" data-paper-title="MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-msn-56fd8b3f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-008ce07355140f61">Why put capacity in MSN memory slots instead of a fully dense network?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsn">MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dense models typically activate all parameters. Memory stores more values but reads few slots, so compute need not grow proportionally. Product keys organize addresses across two axes and a gate fuses values. Sparse reads do not remove maintenance cost or guarantee useful knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieving four files is cheaper than reading an archive, provided the routing finds the right files.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07526">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.07526-msn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-008ce07355140f61">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msn" data-paper-title="MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8c4d706cf2e88507">How does two-axis Product-Key Memory in MSN add capacity while reading little knowledge per query?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsn">MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A slot combines one key from each axis. Summed similarities rank combinations, only a few values are read, and a gate fuses them into the dense backbone. Stored capacity does not all become active compute, and useful routing still matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Two sets of 100 keys address 10,000 slots, but one request reads the four most relevant ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07526">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.07526-msn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c4d706cf2e88507">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msn" data-paper-title="MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b30c3fb7efee183">How does top-k PKM activation differ from a dense soft mixture over every expert?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsn">MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A dense mixture usually evaluates all experts before weighting. PKM finds high-scoring key pairs and reads selected values, leaving most slots inactive. Search and memory access still cost time, and hard selection can miss evidence. Total-to-active parameter ratio does not predict measured latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reading four of 10,000 slots differs from running 100 experts, but scattered reads can offset lower FLOPs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07526">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.07526-msn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b30c3fb7efee183">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:msn" data-paper-title="MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c06429233f8f31d0">Why preserve unique slot IDs and deduplicate top-k two-axis combinations in MSN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Amsn">MSN: A Memory-based Sparse Activation Scaling Framework for Large-scale Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin Search</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both axis addresses identify the slot; the summed similarity is a score, not an ID. Duplicate slots overweight one value. Match value width to the backbone and define short or empty selections. Local genre and transition writes are public proxies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: (2,3) and (3,2) are different slots despite the same index sum, and a duplicate (2,3) is not independent knowledge.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07526">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.07526-msn/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c06429233f8f31d0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nontp" data-paper-title="Not Only NTP: Extending Training Signal Coverage for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-nontp-bd610948" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-56b178d9e31f5503">Why add NONTP auxiliary modules only during training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anontp">Not Only NTP: Extending Training Signal Coverage for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TCL and TDL teach long-range and cross-domain signals to the backbone without future teachers or extra branches at serving time. Richer supervision is not uniformly better, especially with weak domain labels and short histories. Future targets are not available online.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Train for a trajectory several steps ahead but serve with the current history and original item head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12277">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12277-nontp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56b178d9e31f5503">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nontp" data-paper-title="Not Only NTP: Extending Training Signal Coverage for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d443595c80ba49d">Which two kinds of locality do TCL and TDL address in NONTP next-token prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anontp">Not Only NTP: Extending Training Signal Coverage for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TCL predicts a later EMA-teacher state, extending immediate next-step supervision. TDL predicts the target through a shared item head from earlier cross-domain states, helping sparse domains. Both are training-only; inference stays on the original backbone and cannot read future states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Before a lamp purchase, TCL teaches longer trajectories and TDL uses preceding home-content behavior. Serving sees only events already observed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12277">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12277-nontp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d443595c80ba49d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nontp" data-paper-title="Not Only NTP: Extending Training Signal Coverage for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ea47c7bf8e79cb75">How is TCL&#x27;s EMA teacher more stable than a direct online future-state target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anontp">Not Only NTP: Extending Training Signal Coverage for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>EMA smooths updates and gives a stopped-gradient target rather than two sides chasing each other. Future state remains training-only; use other users as negatives rather than mislabeling nearby same-user interests. Stability does not ensure correctness and can preserve old biases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A slow teacher changes less than a recent online update, but a consistently popularity-biased teacher is still biased.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12277">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12277-nontp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ea47c7bf8e79cb75">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:nontp" data-paper-title="Not Only NTP: Extending Training Signal Coverage for Generative Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-e76a922081830518">Why must TDL use pre-target cross-domain history and the same item head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Anontp">Not Only NTP: Extending Training Signal Coverage for Generative Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meituan</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Time order prevents leakage, domain mismatch supplies cross-business transfer, and averaging into the shared NTP head trains the target item space directly. Skip empty groups rather than inventing labels; an independent head is not the same transfer interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Predict a shopping target from earlier other-domain states, not videos afterward. No cross-domain history means no TDL evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12277">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12277-nontp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e76a922081830518">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemodel" data-paper-title="OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onemodel-224b06a8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-623ba2ebeaea8822">Why map heterogeneous scenario fields into uniform event tokens in OneModel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemodel">OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different businesses log different fields and actions. Scene projections establish a common width and attach scene, action, time, and position before the causal backbone. Shared width does not equal shared meaning; gates and hierarchical states preserve differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A ten-second view and a purchase should not be two untyped IDs. Event metadata tells the model what each action means.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
