</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemodel" data-paper-title="OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-56f6b3788fa8c230">What specialization does SAIM retain after OneModel shares a causal backbone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemodel">OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Scenario projections map heterogeneous events into one history space, but sharing every FFN activation can flatten differences. SAIM conditions shared FFN channels on scene embeddings. Global and recent states separately preserve stable and immediate signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Travel browsing and purchases can share history, while ads and content use different gates and recent flight booking remains in the local state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.18606-onemodel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-56f6b3788fa8c230">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemodel" data-paper-title="OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a72433aecc431d2e">What time scales does OneModel global/local fusion preserve beyond a pooled user state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemodel">OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Global attentive pooling summarizes stable patterns, while recent states retain rapid changes. A single pooled vector may average away new needs. Genre-derived scenes lower density in the proxy; report the negative result without extrapolating it to real cross-business logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Long-term travel and a new renovation need can coexist without years of travel events dominating a single average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.18606-onemodel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a72433aecc431d2e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onemodel" data-paper-title="OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbf522267491af2d">What should generate OneModel&#x27;s SAIM gate, and why not use outcomes after prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonemodel">OneModel: A Unified Foundation for Platform-Scale Multi-Scenario Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use the scenario embedding known at request time to modulate the shared FFN. Outcomes supervise only. Maintain causal masking and correct domain projections. Local genre-derived scenes are proxies, not real recommendation, ad, and merchant logs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An ad-request flag is available now; selecting a gate because the user later purchased leaks future information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18606">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.18606-onemodel/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbf522267491af2d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onepiece" data-paper-title="OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onepiece-1b14efa1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6cb4f874464f620f">Why does OnePiece jointly cover retrieval, clicks, and value?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonepiece">OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cascade stages have distinct labels and independent training can lose transferable clues. Shared context and latent updates model multiple needs, while progressive weights schedule learning. Objectives can conflict; a &#x27;reasoning&#x27; name does not verify language reasoning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Relatedness, click likelihood, and expected value complement one another, but high clicks need not imply purchases.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18091">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.18091-onepiece/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6cb4f874464f620f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onepiece" data-paper-title="OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-10aa9ef73312afbd">How do OnePiece&#x27;s latent blocks and progressive task weights differ from simply summing all losses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonepiece">OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residual blocks repeatedly update contextual state before heads read it. Scheduled weights change which objectives dominate training stages so shared representations adapt to retrieval, click, and value. Both path and order matter; a local proxy does not prove verifiable linguistic reasoning in latent states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Learn relevance before raising purchase-value weight to avoid an early sparse objective dominating basic ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18091">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.18091-onepiece/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-10aa9ef73312afbd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onepiece" data-paper-title="OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d12bd2773766ed64">How does progressive weighting change learning order relative to fixed equal task weights?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonepiece">OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed weights exert the same pressure throughout. A schedule lets basic relevance and harder value objectives converge in stages. This can reduce conflicts or cause forgetting, so inspect stage metrics. Proxy results do not make all curricula superior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Emphasize relevance early and transaction value later; forgetting relevance could yield expensive but unrelated items.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18091">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.18091-onepiece/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d12bd2773766ed64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onepiece" data-paper-title="OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d554085990e57412">How verify OnePiece&#x27;s H(k+1) residual update and αt(k) schedule separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonepiece">OnePiece: Bringing Context Engineering and Reasoning to Industrial Cascade Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Shopee</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One updates contextual state per block, the other weights losses per training stage. Distinguish the two meanings of k and verify both state propagation and applied loss weights. A fixed scorer proxy cannot establish full cascade training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: More blocks do not imply progressive weights, and changing losses does not establish multi-step latent updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.18091">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2509.18091-onepiece/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d554085990e57412">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerank" data-paper-title="OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onerank-a08d1448" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-584c43bca671b73a">Why put OneRank task tokens inside the encoder instead of using them only to select output heads?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerank">OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Conditioning inside layers changes how each task interprets fields before prediction. Private channels retain specialization, so unified inputs do not mean complete sharing. The presence of a token does not prove it is used.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Purchase can read budget early and clicks can read freshness; a late head gets one already compressed representation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.16838-onerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-584c43bca671b73a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerank" data-paper-title="OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1cd8516d4afdddcd">Why retain task-private channels and isolate their gradients inside OneRank&#x27;s unified sequence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerank">OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Task tokens condition shared features but cannot prevent conflicting losses from competing for shared parameters. Private channels add dedicated capacity that other tasks cannot update directly. Shared inputs still exchange evidence, and conflict is controlled at specific paths rather than assumed absent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Clicks value novelty and purchases value reliability. Both share user and item history, but click loss must not overwrite purchase-private features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.16838-onerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1cd8516d4afdddcd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerank" data-paper-title="OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3b19d5509abeb544">What differs between OneRank&#x27;s private channels and MMoE task-specific gates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerank">OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A gate mixes shared experts that other tasks still update. Private channels own task-specific parameters and block other tasks&#x27; gradients. Both retain sharing, not complete independence. The public proxy does not establish that industrial negative transfer is solved.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A purchase gate changes expert weights but clicks can update those experts. Click loss should not change purchase-private parameters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.16838-onerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3b19d5509abeb544">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onerank" data-paper-title="OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-985fc19979a70550">How check that OneRank loss Lj cannot update another task&#x27;s φk without freezing shared θ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonerank">OneRank: Unified Transformer-Native Ranking Architecture for Multi-Task Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Renmin University of China</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Backpropagate one task loss. Other private gradients must be zero; its own private and permitted shared parameters can receive gradients. Detaching the whole backbone loses joint training and detaching only outputs may leave private internal paths. Align parameter groups with tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Click training should preserve purchase-private weights but can update shared fields; zeroing all shared gradients is frozen adaptation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16838">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.16838-onerank/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-985fc19979a70550">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans" data-paper-title="OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onetrans-113b41b8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c23a89463d63552a">Why share S-token weights but use position-specific NS-token weights in OneTrans?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans">OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior events have similar roles, whereas user and item fields are heterogeneous. Joint causal interaction does not make them homogeneous. Position-specific weights cost capacity and must move with field order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Clicks share QKV, but age and price may use separate FFNs. Swapping fields without their mapping treats price like age.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26104">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.26104-onetrans/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c23a89463d63552a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans" data-paper-title="OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a6324bb9639c16d">Why place behavior before non-sequence fields in OneTrans and use different parameter sharing for each?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans">OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Causal order lets later fields read behavior while keeping history independent of later candidates. Homogeneous events share QKV and FFN, while heterogeneous fields use position-specific parameters. Pyramid shortening saves later query work. Reuse still depends on time window, versions, and dependencies.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Reuse earlier click history when swapping a candidate; candidate fields read that history using parameters suited to price and category.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26104">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.26104-onetrans/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a6324bb9639c16d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans" data-paper-title="OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-26773a58a0fb82a3">Where does OneTrans&#x27;s pyramid of S queries save work compared with keeping full length in every layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans">OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Later layers update fewer recent queries, reducing output and interactions. Older evidence can survive through earlier states or legal K/V; it is not dropped from the input or absent everywhere. The small-data head concentration is not generalization evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Read broad history in shallow layers and focus on recent queries later, unlike deleting distant events first.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26104">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.26104-onetrans/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26773a58a0fb82a3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans" data-paper-title="OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc6751d4905424ae">Why do OneTrans NS order and causal masking determine visibility?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans">OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>S-first lets later fields read history while history cannot read later candidates, enabling shared state. Visibility between NS positions depends on the actual mask. Validate history, time encoding, and model versions before reusing cross-request caches, not just user ID.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Move a candidate before history and later events may see it, invalidating the old cache contract.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26104">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2510.26104-onetrans/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc6751d4905424ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans-v2" data-paper-title="OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-onetrans-v2-65020d24" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-298dd87277815a64">Why keep three stages&#x27; own inputs and targets while sharing OneTrans-V2 user context?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans-v2">OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Retrieval, preranking, and fine ranking have different candidate counts and features. Shared causal history saves encoding, while stage-specific tokens preserve constraints and controlled losses transfer knowledge. A stage cannot read another&#x27;s future labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Retrieval sees codes while fine ranking sees item details; shared history does not expose posteriors to retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.28589-onetrans-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-298dd87277815a64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans-v2" data-paper-title="OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6a597373c4b5370">Why share user context but forbid cross-stage token attention in OneTrans-V2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans-v2">OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Three stages can reuse costly behavior encoding while retaining distinct inputs and objectives. Each reads only prior behavior, avoiding downstream or future leakage. Fine-to-pre-ranking knowledge travels through controlled distillation, not unrestricted reads. Local work lacks independent three-stage controls.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: All stages share observed browsing, but retrieval cannot see later clicks or fine-rank labels. Preranking learns from a stopped-gradient teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.28589-onetrans-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6a597373c4b5370">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans-v2" data-paper-title="OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-aab24cdef04fe358">Why aren&#x27;t independent stage attention and fine-to-pre-rank distillation contradictory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans-v2">OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Forward isolation controls serving inputs; training distillation transfers stopped-gradient soft supervision into parameters. It need not expose the fine-ranker online. Runnable stages without an independent three-stage baseline do not establish cascade gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Teach preranking to mimic fine ranking offline. Running fine ranking first on every request defeats ordering and cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.28589-onetrans-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aab24cdef04fe358">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:onetrans-v2" data-paper-title="OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4f365ce2631ae170">Why should OneTrans-V2 decision offsets directly change only decision logits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aonetrans-v2">OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The local test offsets two observable proxy decisions. Given a decision, it should not directly rewrite SID distributions or pre-/fine-rank outputs. This tests interface independence, not unobserved purchase value or ad supply. Proxy thresholds are not CTR/CVR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Raising the discovery offset can change decision likelihood, not add a constant to all fine-rank scores.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28589">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.28589-onetrans-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4f365ce2631ae170">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinfm" data-paper-title="PinFM: Foundation Model for User Activity Sequences at a Billion-scale Visual Discovery Platform" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-pinfm-c653f7d8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-73e242cb9a591ae2">Why combine next-, multi-, and future-token objectives in PinFM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinfm">PinFM: Foundation Model for User Activity Sequences at a Billion-scale Visual Discovery Platform</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The immediate item, future window, and future from a specified position supply distinct time scales, helping learn more than recency before transfer. Future labels are training-only. Cross-scenario pretraining can negatively transfer despite being a foundation model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Next click teaches immediate intent, a window teaches coexisting interests, and later targets add long-term direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12704">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2507.12704-pinfm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-73e242cb9a591ae2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinfm" data-paper-title="PinFM: Foundation Model for User Activity Sequences at a Billion-scale Visual Discovery Platform" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4eaf16c90d354ace">How does PinFM DCAT retain early candidate fusion without re-encoding user context per item?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinfm">PinFM: Foundation Model for User Activity Sequences at a Billion-scale Visual Discovery Platform</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early fusion lets candidates interact with history internally. DCAT self-attends once over deduplicated context, caches layer K/V, and lets candidate queries read it. Shared state must be candidate-independent. Serving savings and pretraining gains are distinct; retain local negative outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Encode 500 events once for 100 candidates rather than copying all history 100 times, while candidates still read it inside layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12704">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2507.12704-pinfm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4eaf16c90d354ace">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinfm" data-paper-title="PinFM: Foundation Model for User Activity Sequences at a Billion-scale Visual Discovery Platform" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c67c18389f789088">Why does scratch versus pretrained DCAT answer a different question from DCAT versus ordinary Transformer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinfm">PinFM: Foundation Model for User Activity Sequences at a Billion-scale Visual Discovery Platform</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keeping DCAT fixed isolates pretraining, while changing architecture tests cache decomposition or fusion. The selected local pretrained model regressed on test; mathematical DCAT fidelity does not establish pretraining value. Measure serving efficiency separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Training two models with the same architecture differently says nothing about a third architecture that was never tested.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12704">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2507.12704-pinfm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c67c18389f789088">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:pinfm" data-paper-title="PinFM: Foundation Model for User Activity Sequences at a Billion-scale Visual Discovery Platform" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdbf98eb2bd2f065">Why confirm actual context K/V reuse during DCAT full-catalog inference?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apinfm">PinFM: Foundation Model for User Activity Sequences at a Billion-scale Visual Discovery Platform</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute context self-attention once and let candidate layers perform only legal candidate-dependent work. Equal scores do not imply equal execution cost, so check call counts and dependencies. Bind caches to history and version and exclude candidate-conditioned states.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Recomputing history for 1,000 candidates can give the same NDCG while yielding no amortization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12704">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2507.12704-pinfm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdbf98eb2bd2f065">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:poem" data-paper-title="POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-poem-c8eda543" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ed49350b97afd6ab">How do POEM ranks differ from raw CTR or GMV values?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apoem">POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ranks preserve which item comes first within an objective but drop units and magnitude, allowing cross-objective comparisons. They cannot replace all value information, such as one versus a hundred dollars.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: A can have slightly higher CTR but much lower GMV. The two rank directions omit &#x27;slightly&#x27; and &#x27;much.&#x27;</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29946">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.29946-poem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ed49350b97afd6ab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:poem" data-paper-title="POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-47020eb5235815f6">Why does POEM build a partial order from multiple objectives rather than order training sequences chronologically?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apoem">POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Event time does not measure present-request preference. POEM aggregates objective-relative candidate ranks into a partial order for supervision. Disagreement need not become a unique rank. Existing objective judgments are not independent unbiased user preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: An item viewed later can be preferred by click and purchase objectives. Use that relation instead of mistaking browse chronology for preference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29946">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.29946-poem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47020eb5235815f6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:poem" data-paper-title="POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2b4709f97e0a86d4">What can POEM majority comparison lose versus retaining all conflicting evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apoem">POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A majority compresses goals to one direction and can lose strongly opposed minority objectives and margins. A partial-order focus differs from representing both sides. The mechanism comparison does not prove universal performance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Three weak votes for A beat two strong votes for B, hiding the purchase margin.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29946">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.29946-poem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2b4709f97e0a86d4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:poem" data-paper-title="POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-54078c13921f4ddf">Why check POEM pairwise majorities for ties or cycles rather than assume a total order?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Apoem">POEM: Partial-Order Enhanced Real-Time Sequential Modeling for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A can beat B, B beat C, and C beat A, and ties have no unique direction. If a sequence is needed, apply a defined stable rule and record it. Never use test labels to choose a favorable ordering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Illustration: Breaking a cycle by item ID is an additional rule, not evidence that candidates had a consistent true order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29946">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.29946-poem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54078c13921f4ddf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:rankmixer" data-paper-title="RankMixer: Scaling Up Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-rankmixer-298d1226" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-558c5d17470ec022">Which attention does RankMixer replace?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Arankmixer">RankMixer: Scaling Up Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance / Douyin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It replaces attention for heterogeneous field interactions, not necessarily independent behavior sequence encoding. TokenMix and specialized FFNs process fields after feature extraction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>History attention can extract photography interest before mixing it with price and item fields.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
