</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:slimper" data-paper-title="SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-slimper-ce7fc963" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c31fdda2ede9afd6">Does not updating all history at each SlimPer layer eliminate relationships between adjacent behaviors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aslimper">SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Section 2.5 adds local context when tokenizing events, for example via convolution or windowed attention. Later layers repeatedly read those tokens and update a fixed bank. This avoids deep all-pairs history interaction, not every historical relation. Fixed slots cap intermediate state; storing and reading inputs still grows with history length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search, compare, and add-to-cart events can get local context before candidate-specific slots read them, without rewriting the full history at every layer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c31fdda2ede9afd6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:slimper" data-paper-title="SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-4a13e5753d9c783b">How does SlimPer keep its knowledge base fixed in size while reading the full history at every layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aslimper">SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Only a small set of candidate-specific slots is updated. Original user tokens are revisited as read-only evidence. Select retrieves relevant evidence, Match compares it with templates, and Refine updates slots. The full hidden history does not propagate between layers. Candidates share user encodings, but each evolves its own knowledge base rather than using one final interest vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shoe and camera candidates can read the same purchase records but organize size and photography signals in separate banks. Slots updated for shoes must not be reused unchanged for cameras.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4a13e5753d9c783b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:slimper" data-paper-title="SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8469615c85e200f">If SlimPer already selects evidence with attention, why explicitly dot-product it with knowledge templates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aslimper">SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select builds queries from the current bank and aggregates a few user evidence vectors. Match compares those vectors with templates from the same bank, yielding a query-by-template relevance matrix. Refine updates knowledge from these explicit relations rather than treating the aggregate as final interest. Retrieval and aspect-specific relevance are separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For running shoes, Select finds running distances and sizes. Match evaluates comfort and intended use separately. Finding evidence does not tell which candidate aspect it supports.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8469615c85e200f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:slimper" data-paper-title="SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-85f55baa2ea8d44b">Why is SlimPer not just a sequence encoder when compared with HSTU or LONGER?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aslimper">SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SlimPer models user–item relevance. Its knowledge base also receives item and cross features, and each Select–Match–Refine layer forms a personalized ranking state. A matched comparison needs candidate interactions and the task head, not only a user-sequence vector.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two candidates can produce different knowledge bases from the same history. Do not compare them solely to a candidate-independent encoder output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-85f55baa2ea8d44b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:slimper" data-paper-title="SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8b4dfeda1146dd5b">Once SlimPer fixes the knowledge-base size, can later layers stop reading long histories?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aslimper">SlimPer: Make Personalization Model Slim and Smart</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Each layer queries shared original tokens. It saves updates to N history states at each layer but still accesses KN query–history pairs. Short MovieLens runs, AdamW, and analytical element counts do not reproduce production QPS or Shampoo results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A small bank must still revisit the evidence; it is not a one-shot compression that discards the history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12281">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.12281-slimper/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8b4dfeda1146dd5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-ranking" data-paper-title="SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sort-ranking-bed02966" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e9bf08ccb75e4b5">Why isn&#x27;t SORT Ranking simply a language Transformer for recommendations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-ranking">SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Industrial fields, tokenization, attention, FFNs, and hardware layout are co-designed to replace DLRM. Generic residual equations are not the full system.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sparse categorical features are not prepared like natural-language words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03988-sort-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e9bf08ccb75e4b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-ranking" data-paper-title="SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-a030a6e6a420cbd7">Why co-design tokenization, attention, and FFNs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-ranking">SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heterogeneous fields and long histories need appropriate token interfaces, information flow, and tokenwise capacity. Compression changes resource allocation. Local mechanisms do not establish full DLRM replacement throughput or quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Organize age, category, and history rather than treating them all as ordinary text tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03988-sort-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a030a6e6a420cbd7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-ranking" data-paper-title="SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2bf52e7b5dfc4fcf">How does a ranking Transformer differ from a traditional DLRM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-ranking">SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token interaction handles features and histories; DLRMs commonly combine embeddings, explicit interactions, and MLPs. Cost and feature processing affect deployment, not names alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The same IDs can interact at different stages with different compute reuse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03988">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.03988-sort-ranking/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2bf52e7b5dfc4fcf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sort-ranking" data-paper-title="SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-654aff3c4fd7e4fa">Does local residual MHA/FFN demonstrate industrial compression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asort-ranking">SORT: A Systematically Optimized Ranking Transformer for Industrial-scale Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba International Digital Commerce</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed public candidates exercise core paths without private features, production scale, or kernels. Model structure alone is not measured QPS or uplift.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sparsectr" data-paper-title="Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-sparsectr-7769ddba" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-66b713ab69ef6033">Why chunk histories using personal time gaps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asparsectr">Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Event counts do not separate dense sessions from long breaks. Adaptive chunks follow individual pace, with global, transition, and local attention handling different scales.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A burst today and a revisit next month should not be grouped solely because events are adjacent.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17836">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.17836-sparsectr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-66b713ab69ef6033">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sparsectr" data-paper-title="Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-132c0a2e3ff407c5">Why combine time-adaptive chunks with global, transition, and local attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asparsectr">Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal event counts may span minutes or months. Time grouping respects personal rhythm; three routes capture overview, shifts, and fine details. Relative time encodes intervals/cycles but can miss sudden or sparse interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separate a furniture browsing burst from later supply shopping while modeling the transition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17836">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.17836-sparsectr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-132c0a2e3ff407c5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sparsectr" data-paper-title="Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-88c258ca85063872">How does three-path EvoAttention differ from a sparse local window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asparsectr">Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local reads details, global chunks represent cross-period interests, and transition paths model changes. Time biases capture intervals and calendar cues, not causal guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weekend patterns can correlate with interest without causing clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.17836">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.17836-sparsectr/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88c258ca85063872">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:sparsectr" data-paper-title="Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-adfe96136481aa5b">Do local time features replace production chronology?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Asparsectr">Unleashing the Potential of Sparse Attention on Long-term Behaviors for CTR Prediction</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Institute of Software, Chinese Academy of Sciences</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Fixed MovieLens tests chunks and biases only. Sort pre-request events, align biases with valid masks, and exclude future labels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shared wrong threshold can impose identical chunks on users with different rhythms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:specformer" data-paper-title="SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<span id="paper-recommendation-specformer-bc626a07" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-af3ed7d85d90e349">Why inspect singular spectra for representation collapse?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspecformer">SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Concentration in a few directions reduces diversity. Spectral softening changes relative singular values; spectral positional residuals affect attention. A flatter spectrum is not task evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Nearly parallel user vectors struggle to distinguish interests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24025-specformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-af3ed7d85d90e349">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:specformer" data-paper-title="SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2c07d9b7ab232c29">Why can spectral softening counter collapse?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspecformer">SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dominant singular modes concentrate tokens and limit deep interaction. Softening reduces disparity and spectral residuals give attention structural cues. This is not lossless equalization; weak modes can be noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reduce popularity dominance so genre directions can matter without assuming every weak direction helps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24025">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24025-specformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2c07d9b7ab232c29">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:specformer" data-paper-title="SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7082029b0c37a3e7">How does spectral softening differ from L2-normalizing embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aspecformer">SpecFormer: Mitigating Embedding and Attention Collapse via Spectral-Aware Transformer for Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Zhejiang University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Unit norms control individual lengths, not collective directional spectrum. Singular-value transforms redistribute subspace energy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Unit-length vectors can still all point the same way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tm20k" data-paper-title="Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tm20k-e967dab7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-016bcc070aa74faf">Why let TM20K&#x27;s teacher keep all tokens while the student merges?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atm20k">Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Full-token attention and ranking provide detail for distillation. Student compression controls serving budget but does not preserve every event.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teacher reads 20,000 events; student learns from grouped summaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.07055-tm20k/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-016bcc070aa74faf">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tm20k" data-paper-title="Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-74a2478da4c70ed5">Why merge as sum/√n and distill a full-token teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atm20k">Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Grouping bounds tokens, and square-root normalization moderates sum growth while retaining group-size effects. Attention and ranking distillation approximate useful fine relations without reversing compression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Merge four browses into one; teacher sees internal relationships the student cannot recover exactly.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.07055-tm20k/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74a2478da4c70ed5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tm20k" data-paper-title="Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4fc9b1e5b55bbd3a">How does sum/√n differ from average pooling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atm20k">Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mean divides by n; square-root normalization retains different energy scaling as group size changes, depending on correlation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeating a vector changes the two resulting norms differently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.07055">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.07055-tm20k/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4fc9b1e5b55bbd3a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tm20k" data-paper-title="Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-78f74f3d70d3c699">How align attention distillation across different lengths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atm20k">Teacher Retains Full Tokens, Student Merges Efficiently: TM20K for E-Commerce Sequence Modeling in Ad Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Map teacher positions into student groups; do not subtract mismatched matrices. Preserve masks and sizes. Local work lacks production long histories and traffic.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Specify which four teacher entries correspond to one merged slot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tmallgs" data-paper-title="TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tmallgs-f2b12094" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c3dfd8bedd01d8cd">Why learn field-specific Q/K/V in TMallGS?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atmallgs">TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Queries, user history, and item fields have different semantics and noise. Field projections, saliency, and gates shape interactions by reliability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A search term and years of browsing need not use one projection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13398">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.13398-tmallgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c3dfd8bedd01d8cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tmallgs" data-paper-title="TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d7c6269d0941de88">Why combine field-specific Q/K/V, noise gates, and layer supervision?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atmallgs">TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate projections address heterogeneous distributions, saliency and gates control noisy interactions, FiLM injects content, and intermediate loss guides deep learning. Gains cannot be attributed just to more heads.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Downweight an accidental click while preserving an explicit search term and train intermediate relevance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13398">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.13398-tmallgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d7c6269d0941de88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tmallgs" data-paper-title="TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-37475999840701e5">How does FiLM differ from concatenating content features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atmallgs">TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FiLM generates per-coordinate scale and bias; concatenation passes features onward. Progressive supervision also assigns intermediate targets, not just one MLP.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Content can emphasize hidden directions rather than merely add columns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13398">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.13398-tmallgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-37475999840701e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tmallgs" data-paper-title="TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-229c564ec8014c24">Does a very large relative NDCG gain establish a stable win?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atmallgs">TMallGS: Scaling Unified Feature and Sequence Modeling for Generative E-commerce Search</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group of Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Absolute hits are few and one seed with a low denominator inflates percentages. The run exercises field, gate, FiLM, bias, and intermediate training paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny absolute improvement can have a huge percentage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13398">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.13398-tmallgs/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-229c564ec8014c24">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenmixer-large" data-paper-title="TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-tokenmixer-large-095f089c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e02f63426f1ac85">Does parameter-free mixing make the whole TokenMixer-Large parameter-free?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenmixer-large">TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Mix/revert are fixed rearrangements; headwise and tokenwise SwiGLU, deep residuals, and auxiliary losses still learn.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Channel shuffling is fixed, but the FFNs processing channels train.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.06563-tokenmixer-large/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e02f63426f1ac85">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenmixer-large" data-paper-title="TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0857a64a43674f">Why use headwise SwiGLU after mixing and tokenwise SwiGLU after revert?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenmixer-large">TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The former learns cross-token combinations from rearranged channels; the latter refines restored per-token states. Residual intervals and intermediate supervision support depth. Rearrangement moves information but does not learn interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Mix price and preference channels, learn interactions, then restore fields for token-specific processing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.06563-tokenmixer-large/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0857a64a43674f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenmixer-large" data-paper-title="TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-411f9977314d5723">What does mix–headFFN–revert add over tokenwise FFN?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenmixer-large">TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rearrangement exposes slices from different tokens to a nonlinear head transform, then restores layout. It is not dynamic attention, and one small gain cannot replace all attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Each token can receive transformed evidence from other tokens after reverting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.06563-tokenmixer-large/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-411f9977314d5723">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tokenmixer-large" data-paper-title="TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-456741bae5caa17a">What can the local RankMixer comparison establish?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atokenmixer-large">TokenMixer-Large: Scaling Up Large Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Match width, depth, negatives, and steps, but the result is small single-seed and lacks full attention controls. Bind FFNs to mixed positions and preserve revert order.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The first mixed head need not be the first original feature slot.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.06563">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.06563-tokenmixer-large/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-456741bae5caa17a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transact-v2" data-paper-title="TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-transact-v2-c124d4cb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b825891732ff4c2e">Why combine lifelong and recent histories in TransAct V2?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransact-v2">TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate retrieval finds relevant older evidence, while recent history captures immediate intent. One Transformer fuses both with candidates early.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A current browse and a similar older interest can both support a candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.02267-transact-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b825891732ff4c2e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transact-v2" data-paper-title="TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-38858cbd67f8f10d">Why keep raw recent events and add Next Action Loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransact-v2">TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Candidate matching retrieves old evidence but can miss emerging intent. Keep recent events and fuse with retrieved history. NAL learns next positive action beyond CTR; missed remote events and serving performance remain separate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tent candidate finds old camping while raw history shows new family-travel interest.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.02267-transact-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-38858cbd67f8f10d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transact-v2" data-paper-title="TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5693f8fb31713bda">How does guaranteed recent retention differ from full-history top-k?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransact-v2">TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It keeps fresh behavior even with low similarity, while other positions come from candidate search. Extra context costs compute; gains depend on data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A new interest may not rank highly under an old similarity model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02267">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2506.02267-transact-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5693f8fb31713bda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transact-v2" data-paper-title="TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<h2 id="qa-10ca6a9f91815dd7">Can Next Action Loss labels enter the current input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransact-v2">TransAct V2: Lifelong User Action Sequence Modeling on Pinterest Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Pinterest</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Next positive behavior is supervision only; input reads the past, and negatives must be valid. Local model scope excludes production SKUT/request dedup and throughput.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transx" data-paper-title="TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-transx-58683026" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ef59c1c3050aa984">Why split behavior and request streams?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransx">TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cache global/local historical states asynchronously, then let short candidate requests cross-attend. Share only candidate-independent portions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several candidates read one user cache but retain separate matching.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28940">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28940-transx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ef59c1c3050aa984">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transx" data-paper-title="TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f63260b88299146b">Why cache global/local behavior and cross-attend only from the short service stream?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransx">TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Behavior changes slower than requests, allowing historical encoding amortization. Global represents overall interests, local recent detail. Cache building/refresh still cost work, and candidate-dependent states are not public user caches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reuse long history across opens and refresh local data without re-encoding years per candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28940">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.28940-transx/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f63260b88299146b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transx" data-paper-title="TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-89587d43acc170b5">How does shared multi-cutoff pooling compare with independent pooling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransx">TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Merge softmax statistics to reuse prefix work, with equivalent forward and gradients. This is compute reuse, not a changed score. Base, Retrieval, and Ranking are distinct production tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shared pooling should match independent computation on the same input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 补充核心公式, 补充报告效果与本地验收. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:transx" data-paper-title="TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-78624c18f023b1ae">Why combine duplicate sparse row gradients before squaring?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atransx">TransX: Scaling Transformer-based Recommendation via Behavioral and Serving Stream Crossings</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · LinkedIn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Squaring is nonlinear: sum logical-step gradients first. Small A100 tensors verify this rule, not the 32-H200 system or an upgraded adapter grade.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Opposite gradients should cancel before the square.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 补充核心公式, 补充报告效果与本地验收. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4b28124dc59a54c0">Why serialize cross-page activity as a Tubi user story?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atubifm">TubiFM: Unified Item, Carousel, and Search Ranking for Streaming Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tubi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item, carousel, and search activity relates across the journey. One history and task prompts share evidence while preserving task-specific ranking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Search then browse a collection to explain what film the viewer now wants.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:tubifm" data-paper-title="TubiFM: Unified Item, Carousel, and Search Ranking for Streaming Discovery" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-23cac2c087366ab8">Why use one cross-page story and task prompts for item, carousel, and search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atubifm">TubiFM: Unified Item, Carousel, and Search Ranking for Streaming Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tubi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate page models miss links between events. One sequence shares the journey, while prompts identify scoring targets. Shared input does not equal shared objectives or calibrated candidate types.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use suspense search and carousel browsing as common context, then specify whether ranking films, rows, or results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23702">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.23702-tubifm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-23cac2c087366ab8">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tubi</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atubifm">TubiFM: Unified Item, Carousel, and Search Ranking for Streaming Discovery</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tubi</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twin-v2" data-paper-title="TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<span id="paper-recommendation-twin-v2-72f26bc8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9b5a1473f6d5e8e0">Why compress lifelong history into sized virtual items?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwin-v2">TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-event matching over millions is expensive. Offline hierarchy summarizes groups and tracks size, then online retrieval and ranking read relevant clusters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Many repeated events should differ from one isolated event.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twin-v2" data-paper-title="TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-646dc7ef8fc54339">Why build sized virtual items before candidate-related retrieval?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwin-v2">TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Offline clustering compresses repeated events. GSU retrieves relevant clusters and ESU performs size-aware interactions without naively duplicating large groups. Rare details may disappear.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Represent years of similar shoe browsing with a count rather than recomputing attention on thousands of events.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2407.16357-twin-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-646dc7ef8fc54339">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twin-v2" data-paper-title="TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-041577c428d8fcae">How does cluster retrieval differ from SIM raw-behavior search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwin-v2">TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cluster search filters prototypes before finer interaction; raw retrieval selects original behaviors. Compression changes coverage, accuracy, and cost, with possible rare-detail loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A large cluster may hide a niche event that raw search can still find.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.16357">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2407.16357-twin-v2/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-041577c428d8fcae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:twin-v2" data-paper-title="TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d3fdc1036f68dd31">Does public full-catalog ranking verify million-event serving?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Atwin-v2">TWIN V2: Scaling Ultra-Long User Behavior Sequence Modeling for Enhanced CTR Prediction at Kuaishou</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
