<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ultra-hstu" data-paper-title="Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-ultra-hstu-194b1e9b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fed2ecbf8d76051">Why add landmarks beyond the local ULTRA-HSTU window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aultra-hstu">Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local attention preserves detail; sparse landmarks connect distant behavior. LBSL widens deeper layers. Sparse access is not lossless full-HSTU equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read recent events individually and use representative remote positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.16986-ultra-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fed2ecbf8d76051">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ultra-hstu" data-paper-title="Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-11dc09f7eb43dcda">Why combine local windows, landmarks, and increasing layer reach?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aultra-hstu">Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed local masks lose remote paths and full attention is expensive. Sparse landmarks provide global connections, wider deeper windows integrate more context, and mixture/system changes support scale. Efficiency depends on windows, landmark counts, and kernels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shallow layers read recent clicks, while landmarks and deeper layers connect older interests without recovering every event.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.16986-ultra-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11dc09f7eb43dcda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ultra-hstu" data-paper-title="Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c16315fe2bbd6913">How do semi-local attention and deeper wider windows differ from one fixed window?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aultra-hstu">Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deeper layers gain wider direct access, while fixed windows retain identical local connections per layer. Effective reach also depends on stacking and landmarks; one formula does not cover mixture, precision, and systems changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read a visit closely in shallow layers, then relate cross-visit interests deeper.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.16986-ultra-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c16315fe2bbd6913">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:ultra-hstu" data-paper-title="Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-265d87b066b4fd3e">Can a 48-event ablation prove the 16K production scaling law?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aultra-hstu">Bending the Scaling Law Curve in Large-Scale Recommendation Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It lacks 18-layer production models, dynamic topology, FP8 kernels, and private logs. Scaling needs matched runs across lengths and hardware measurement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A max-length setting of 16000 does not test long history if only dozens are loaded.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16986">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2602.16986-ultra-hstu/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-265d87b066b4fd3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniformer" data-paper-title="UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-uniformer-655acc49" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a1a76d598f2841bc">Why tokenize feature roles and tasks in UniFormer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniformer">UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One interaction interface carries candidate-independent, candidate-dependent, and task-specific states. Tokenization preserves role distinctions rather than flattening all fields.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>User history, current product, and click objective each get appropriate tokens.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.27058-uniformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a1a76d598f2841bc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniformer" data-paper-title="UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b79ebda446d84c88">Why distinguish candidate-independent, candidate-dependent, and task tokens before unified interactions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniformer">UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>They encode common user state, current match, and prediction objective respectively. Explicit roles ease scaling, but joint interactions can make states candidate-dependent; reuse needs masks and architecture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A shared age token is reusable, but a state containing one candidate&#x27;s price is not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.27058-uniformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b79ebda446d84c88">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniformer" data-paper-title="UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-8301b52622a60f8a">What is the trade-off versus separate models per task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniformer">UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shared interactions can transfer signal and ease maintenance; task tokens condition predictions. Parameter sharing can still cause interference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Viewing features may help clicks but conflict with commerce goals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.27058-uniformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8301b52622a60f8a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniformer" data-paper-title="UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-52f840ed13b3837f">How avoid token misalignment locally?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniformer">UniFormer: Efficient and Unified Model-Centric Scaling for Industrial Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Match role, position, and valid mask to fields, and have each task head read its own state. MovieLens lacks industrial fields and serving.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Task A reading task B&#x27;s token is wrong despite matching shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27058">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2606.27058-uniformer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52f840ed13b3837f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unirec" data-paper-title="UniRec: Cross-Stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Optimization for Cascaded Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-unirec-cd2efe22" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-505d1682319fe757">Why keep two separate pre-ranking and ranking towers?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunirec">UniRec: Cross-Stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Optimization for Cascaded Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Their features, candidate scales, and latency differ. Share some embeddings and align downstream preference through training, without exposing expensive online ranking input upstream.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Pre-ranking learns fine-ranker preference from supervision, not its full feature set.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11052">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11052-unirec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-505d1682319fe757">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unirec" data-paper-title="UniRec: Cross-Stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Optimization for Cascaded Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0c25f39de037db51">Why preserve both directions for one pair in CPPA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunirec">UniRec: Cross-Stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Optimization for Cascaded Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Objectives can disagree, and a majority loses strength and minority signal. Both softplus penalties remain, CAPP selects confident directions, and grouped KL limits drift. Downstream supervision is training-only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clicks favor A while purchases favor B; majority voting can hide the purchase signal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11052">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11052-unirec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0c25f39de037db51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unirec" data-paper-title="UniRec: Cross-Stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Optimization for Cascaded Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dee5064fb3689990">How does CPPA differ from majority-voting among objectives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunirec">UniRec: Cross-Stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Optimization for Cascaded Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Opposing evidence contributes to two softplus terms rather than discarding the minority. CAPP chooses confident directed pairs and AGRR controls group drift separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Clicks can prefer A and watch time B; retain both directions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11052">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11052-unirec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dee5064fb3689990">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:unirec" data-paper-title="UniRec: Cross-Stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Optimization for Cascaded Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7061b74a6ba3a598">How keep cross-stage gradient isolation and AGRR evidence separate from pruning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Aunirec">UniRec: Cross-Stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Optimization for Cascaded Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Cross-stage alignment uses survivors and freezes the fine-ranker direction. AGRR builds grouped KL targets from unpruned inputs, not centered scores. Document variance and quantile ties.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Computing evidence after pruning changes the distribution AGRR should see.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11052">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2609.11052-unirec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7061b74a6ba3a598">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniscale" data-paper-title="UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-uniscale-5256c0f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18cbfa80cab3f0a4">Why expand both data space and model capacity?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniscale">UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Larger models still face exposure bias; more data can also exceed current capacity. ES³ expands beyond exposure, HHSFT fuses sources, and capacity must remain deployable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adding unexposed examples differs from adding layers to old exposure data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.24226-uniscale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18cbfa80cab3f0a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniscale" data-paper-title="UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f29a5b9c1c823d5f">Why expand exposure-external data and train hierarchically rather than only grow the model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniscale">UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>More parameters can overfit limited exposure. Broader data expands coverage and hierarchical fusion treats heterogeneous quality appropriately. Verify synthetic/unexposed reliability; more data need not reduce bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Add unseen categories without giving weak labels the same weight as verified clicks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.24226-uniscale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f29a5b9c1c823d5f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniscale" data-paper-title="UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5d1802efe29e31aa">Are unexposed examples equivalent to random negatives?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniscale">UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Sources and label reliability differ. Not exposed is not disliked, and full-space expansion does not automatically remove selection bias.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A user who never saw an item cannot be assumed not to click it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.24226-uniscale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5d1802efe29e31aa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uniscale" data-paper-title="UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-49ea328e0fbe6bb4">Does local UniScale gated FFN represent the full ES³ data pipeline?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auniscale">UniScale: Synergistic Entire Space Data and Model Scaling for Search Ranking</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Taobao &amp; Tmall Group / Alibaba</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It tests heterogeneous branches, not private full-space sampling, production models, or cheap deployment. Audit source labels, splits, and mixing weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Working FFNs do not prove reliable exposure-external data generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24226">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2603.24226-uniscale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-49ea328e0fbe6bb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uxsid" data-paper-title="UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<span id="paper-recommendation-uxsid-c8fb3e15" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f96582456061914a">Why share UxSID memory by user and target SID?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auxsid">UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-item retrieval is expensive and one user-only summary is too coarse. Similar first-level SID targets share memory, trading cache cost for targeting without assuming identical preferences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several shoes can reuse interest memory while retaining item differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09040">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.09040-uxsid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f96582456061914a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uxsid" data-paper-title="UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-79650491f8323060">Why share memory by first-level target SID instead of per-item or all-item compression?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auxsid">UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Grouping amortizes full history while retaining target sensitivity. Global SID response gates anchor probing; independent PFFNs and orthogonality mitigate collapse. Within-group details can still be flattened.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Camping items share one camping memory while cameras use another.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09040">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.09040-uxsid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-79650491f8323060">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uxsid" data-paper-title="UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-c5172297d44da3dd">Why are global and local probes not duplicate attention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auxsid">UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Query full history for a global response, gate the target SID, then read compressed anchors. The inputs differ; anchor-only loses global modulation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Determine overall category interest before inspecting individual anchors.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09040">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.09040-uxsid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c5172297d44da3dd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:uxsid" data-paper-title="UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3502ab9fa810ccda">What details matter for per-anchor PFFN and orthogonality?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Auxsid">UxSID: Semantic-Aware User Interests Modeling for Ultra-Long Sequence</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Kuaishou</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Give anchors independent PFFNs and normalize orthogonality by the whole matrix&#x27;s squared L2 norm, not row cosine norms. Local two-level k-means/residual quantization is not LETTER.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sharing one FFN changes anchor specialization even at matching shapes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09040">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2605.09040-uxsid/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3502ab9fa810ccda">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:whale" data-paper-title="WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<span id="paper-recommendation-whale-9ea1c28b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-263367f367c9a7fa">Why exchange information between Wukong and HSTU at each layer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awhale">WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse high-order fields and behavior sequences co-evolve instead of meeting only at final concatenation. Coupling may also cause interference.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Attributes affect sequence interest and sequence states contextualize feature interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17017-whale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-263367f367c9a7fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:whale" data-paper-title="WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0dbf74a57516dd91">Why exchange Wukong and HSTU state bidirectionally at every layer rather than only at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awhale">WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Field interactions model high-order combinations and sequences capture evolving behavior. Cross-attention lets each guide later processing by the other. This adds dependencies and cost, not reusable user-only caching; local evidence is scaled public evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weekend context can focus sequence attention on camping, then updated interests inform price/category interactions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17017">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.17017-whale/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0dbf74a57516dd91">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:whale" data-paper-title="WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfe5edc9b606fe28">How does bidirectional cross-attention differ from late fusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awhale">WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Late-fusion paths stay independent until the end. Intermediate cross-attention changes both state streams and adds dependency costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Layer two can already read features and change later behavior modeling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awhale">WHALE: A Scalable Unified Model for Recommendation with Wukong-HSTU Architecture</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Platforms, Inc.</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wide-deep" data-paper-title="Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<span id="paper-recommendation-wide-deep-604050a0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-44139f39f329ea5a">Why keep linear and deep paths together?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awide-deep">Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Wide memorizes sparse observed crosses; deep embeddings generalize to unseen combinations. One jointly trained logit combines them, rather than alternating independent services.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Memorize frequent combinations and generalize related new ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/1606.07792-wide-deep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-44139f39f329ea5a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wide-deep" data-paper-title="Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc8a20781ba57a95">Why train crosses and deep features jointly rather than average independent scores?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awide-deep">Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both contribute one logit and share objective gradients, allowing complementary learning. Handcrafted crosses have limited coverage and deep generalization can be wrong.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Wide memorizes a frequent user–category cross while deep transfers to related new combinations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/1606.07792-wide-deep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc8a20781ba57a95">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wide-deep" data-paper-title="Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-67f85dbf50d8bc49">How can wide memorization and deep generalization each fail?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awide-deep">Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Memorization misses unseen crosses, while similarity can overgeneralize to incompatible combinations. Capacity should match sparsity and feature engineering.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Semantic similarity does not establish accessory compatibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07792">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/1606.07792-wide-deep/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67f85dbf50d8bc49">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:wide-deep" data-paper-title="Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a065020fe4b932b1">Does local Wide &amp; Deep use production Google Play crosses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Awide-deep">Wide &amp; Deep Learning for Recommender Systems</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. MovieLens replaces private logs and distributed training/serving. Add logits before sigmoid and train jointly, rather than averaging post-sigmoid probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>sigmoid(a+b) generally differs from averaging sigmoid(a) and sigmoid(b).</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:zenith" data-paper-title="Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-bcef87acbc65f178">Why fuse many features into a few Prime Tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azenith">Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North Carolina State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fewer wider tokens reduce interaction count and retain capacity; differentiated attention and independent enhancement counter homogenization. Compression can still lose detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Put sparse fields in several wide slots without making every slot identical.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:zenith" data-paper-title="Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cc81feea6d61f783">Why compress heterogeneous features into wide Prime Tokens and then enhance each separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azenith">Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North Carolina State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Token Fusion trades fewer positions for wider channels; RSA/TMHSA maintain differentiation and SwiGLU or MoE adds role-specific transformations. Check information loss and matched compute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reduce pairwise interactions over 100 fields while preserving meaningful user/item roles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21285">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2601.21285-zenith/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cc81feea6d61f783">Question link</a></p>

<h2 id="qa-7420947d22866257">How does token-specific TSwiGLU differ from shared FFNs?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azenith">Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North Carolina State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent transformations let roles specialize, but add parameters. Match budgets before attributing gains to architecture.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>User and item slots may benefit from different nonlinearities.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="recommendation:zenith" data-paper-title="Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="recommendation" data-theme="recommendation" data-topic="recommendation/history-ranking-backbones">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Search, ads, and recommendation / User histories and ranking backbones</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-df55bed66463ce54">Does local Zenith establish a scaling law?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=recommendation%3Azenith">Zenith: Scaling up Ranking Models for Billion-scale Livestreaming Recommendation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · North Carolina State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Small fixed data exercises fusion, differentiated interaction, and enhancement without production hardware or size. A scaling slope needs matched multi-size curves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A win at one scale does not imply the gap grows with size.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

Should compute go to history–history, candidate–history, or heterogeneous field interactions?

## Takeaway

Identify what interacts. DIN uses candidates to activate relevant history. HSTU exchanges history states across layers. RankMixer uses fixed TokenMix and independent FFNs for heterogeneous features. Long-history compression, mixed sequence and field tokens, sparse attention, and transfer choose what state to keep and when to exchange it. Backbones can complement each other; “Transformer” is not one mechanism.

## Example

A user has a long gardening history and recent cat videos. Cat-food ranking can read recent cat evidence, while garden tools require older interests. Price, context, and profile still need feature crosses. History and fields serve different purposes.

## Common pitfall

Field-token count is not history length; do not compare their complexity tables directly. A cache can be shared only if it is candidate-independent. Public short-history results do not establish industrial long-history gains or serving throughput.

## Reading order

Read DIN for candidate-conditioned interest, HSTU for evolving history states, and RankMixer for field interaction. Then read the [topic deep dive](../../deep-dives/recommendation/history-ranking-backbones.md) for LONGER's short-query path versus SlimPer's fixed user pool. Interpret results within their data and fidelity.

1. [Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction](../../../../reproductions/1706.06978-din/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06978)
2. [Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations](../../../../reproductions/2402.17152-hstu/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152)
3. [RankMixer: Scaling Up Ranking Models in Industrial Recommenders](../../../../reproductions/2507.15551-rankmixer/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.15551)

## Check your understanding

Can a user state that already saw candidate A be reused unchanged as candidate B's shared cache?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Usually no. It depends on A and can contaminate B. Keep a candidate-independent shared path or recompute the candidate-dependent part. A module named user tower is not necessarily reusable.
